subject: Re: Post-call: Unit economics & pricing follow-up (FintechX) - token volumes / $/1M targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps - unit economics / $/1M tokens target

Alex - great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a couple of asks so we can convert this into a scoped proposal: 

Key takeaways
- Use cases discussed: in-app Summarization (primary), Conversational Assist (secondary), Risk Scoring enrichment (low-volume batch).
- Initial ramp: ~50M tokens/month (pilot, Q3). 12-month target: ~400M tokens/month.
- Primary success criteria from your side: predictability of unit cost, ability to hit a target $/1M tokens, and maintain >50% gross margin after inference costs.

Redwood asks / proposed next steps
1) Confirm the 12-month ramp target (50M -> 400M tokens/month). If those change, drop a quick note.
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens you need to make economics work (you mentioned under $20/1M on the call).
3) Share any constraints on model family (open vs. proprietary) or latency SLOs (p95 target).
4) We'll send a short pricing worksheet (attached) with line-item unit economics by feature + example CAC payback scenarios.

High-level pricing context (initial):
- Redwood indicative range for comparable workloads: $15- $30 per 1M tokens (depends on model variant, quantization, and committed capacity).
- For a 400M tokens/month run-rate, committed capacity pricing + caching/quantization typically moves you to the lower end of that range.

Quick unit-econ example (illustrative) - uses your numbers from the call:
- Pilot (50M tokens/mo) -> inference cost at $20/1M = 50 * $20 = $1,000 / month.
- Target (400M tokens/mo) -> inference cost at $20/1M = 400 * $20 = $8,000 / month.
- If you price the feature set at an incremental $2.50 ARPU per MAU / month and target 50k paying MAUs, gross revenue = $125k / month. 
- Inference cost % of revenue (at 400M tokens): $8k / $125k = ~6.4% (well within a healthy margin bucket; enables >50% gross).

CAC / payback framing
- You mentioned a target CAC payback window of ~6-9 months. With the above revenue and cost profile, inference cost is not the primary driver of CAC payback - margins and customer LTV are. We included a couple of worked examples in the attached worksheet.

Next steps:
- If you can confirm the ramp and the $/1M target by EOD Thu (18th), we'll produce a 12-month committed-pricing proposal + canary rollout plan (can include regional fallbacks and model variants).

Attachments: Redwood pricing worksheet (xlsx) and a short pricing proposal (pdf).

Thanks - Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0132
redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechx.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 18:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - unit economics / $/1M tokens target

Thanks, Marissa - solid recap. Confirming the numbers we discussed on the call:
- Pilot expected consumption: ~50M tokens/month for a 6-8 week pilot across Summarization + Assist.
- Scale target: 400M tokens/month within 12 months if pilot metrics (engagement & NPS) hold.
- Target price: ideally <= $20 / 1M tokens to make the unit economics attractive to our CFO. We can stretch to $25 if there are additional SLAs / dedicated capacity assurances.

Some clarifications / answers to your asks:
- Model constraints: prefer open-models for now; however, we'll consider private variants if privacy/latency become blockers.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 400ms for assist flows; summarization can tolerate higher latency (~1s).
- I'll loop in Procurement for legal/SSO/KYC questions - cc'd.

Can you include in the worksheet a simple per-feature cost row (summarization, assist, batch enrichment) so our finance team can map to revenue lines?

- Alex Johnson
Head of Product, FintechX
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - unit economics / $/1M tokens target

Alex - adding a short worked example for the team (so finance sees per-feature rows)

Assumptions (example):
- Token breakdown (monthly at 400M total): Summarization = 60% (240M), Assist = 35% (140M), Batch enrichment = 5% (20M).
- Price assumption: $20 / 1M tokens.

Per-feature inference cost (monthly):
- Summarization: 240 * $20 = $4,800
- Assist: 140 * $20 = $2,800
- Batch enrichment: 20 * $20 = $400
- Total inference cost = $8,000 / month

Per-request cost (avg tokens assuming Summ=300, Assist=120):
- Summarization request cost = (300 / 1,000,000) * $20 = $0.006 / request
- Assist request cost = (120 / 1,000,000) * $20 = $0.0024 / request

If you map those against ARPU per feature, you can see margin by line. Example: if Summarization ARPU = $1.00/mo and Assist ARPU = $0.75/mo with 50k paying MAUs, the inference cost per MAU is small and CAC payback is controlled by acquisition cost, not inference.

I'll attach a spreadsheet with these rows and two CAC payback scenarios (6-month target and 12-month conservative).

- Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement <procurement@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - unit economics / $/1M tokens target

Thanks for the materials. A few procurement items we need before formal pricing discussion: 
1) Can you provide a 12-month committed pricing sheet with three tiers (50M, 200M, 400M tokens/month) and the associated discounts / SLA terms?
2) Please include a short example showing gross margin sensitivity for us (revenue per MAU vs inference cost at each tier).
3) We will need a standard SOC 2 attestation and a sample MSA; please indicate if the pricing assumes Dedicated capacity or Hosted (and any cost delta).

We expect to review the committed-pricing proposal internally Friday and will respond with an initial redline next week.

Procurement
FintechX
